pull.title: coins: warn of low disk space before chainstate compaction
pull.body:
**Problem:** Full chainstate compaction can temporarily require nearly another copy of the database before old files are deleted.

**Fix:** Log automatic full compaction start and finish at info level. Before starting, check the free space on the chainstate filesystem, and if it is below `m_assumed_chain_state_size`, log a warning and skip this compaction. Skipping avoids the temporary extra disk use but leaves obsolete data taking up space.

Fixes #36585

Ideally, start with the one that should be merged first.

> Compaction continues after the warning because postponing cleanup would allow obsolete data to accumulate.

Would it make more sense to just skip compaction if we don't think there's enough free disk space to do it? This would have the tradeoff that some extra data would remain, but it would let users like the issue reporter continue running their node for likely several years without any problems.
I've separated the free-space check from the database operation and unified the compaction logging, as @optout21 suggested in the original PR.

Concept ACK
Left minor comments on the wording of the warning.

coins: skip compaction if disk space is low

Full chainstate compaction can temporarily need about as much extra disk space as the existing database.
Before scheduling it, check the chainstate filesystem using `AssumedChainStateSize()` and the standard free-space reserve, and report available space when deferring compaction.
Deferring avoids the temporary extra disk use but leaves obsolete data taking up space until the operator frees enough space for cleanup.
Skip periodic compaction for in-memory chainstates, which do not need to reclaim disk space.

Co-authored-by: stickies-v <stickies-v@protonmail.com>

events.body: Thanks for the reviews, updated to skip automatic in-memory compaction, use `CheckDiskSpace()` with 50 mb additional overhead, include available space and recovery guidance in the warning, and clarify the release note.

light tACK 2fcfa1dae75ccd11062a6e6073600e67eb20164c

Very new to this part of the code, but this looks good to me. I tested on my own system by:
1. Changing `ShouldCompactChainstate` to always returns true if not in IBD
2. (Almost) filling my disk using `fallocate` :)
3. Calling `bitcoin-cli gettxoutsetinfo` to force flush to disk

And saw the log:
```
2026-11-10T11:49:02Z [warning] Deferring chainstate compaction of /home/daniela/.bitcoin/chainstate: 8.38 GiB free, 14 GiB needed. Free up some space so compaction can run.
```

comments.body:
My understanding of the worst case here is that this happens when all the data is on a single level L, with a very sparse (<32MiB) level L-1 above it. Because L-1 is so sparse, all L-1 files (with keys across the entire L level) get compacted in one go, causing the entire dense level L (~the entire database) to be temporarily copied, correct?

It seems like we're already being more adventurous with our LevelDB usage than we perhaps should be (the `CompactRange` docstring states _"This operation should typically only be invoked by users who understand the underlying implementation."_), but perhaps an alternative approach could be to call `CompactRange` on slices, instead of on the entire (`nullptr`, `nullptr`) range in one go?

Thanks for the hint, we should investigate that - I tried compacting smaller key ranges locally, which reduced peak disk usage in some cases but could still produce large spikes, defeating the purpose. Partial compaction could be investigated separately, but it seems fairly complicated, and I don't think the benefit is worth adding that complexity to this PR.

> [694c535](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36586/changes/694c535312d90e31f5a3c47f4db7cc32cfbb61c0) _coins: skip compaction if disk space is low_:

Additionally logging here the currently observed available space is marginally helpful (guideline: if a log is a result of a decision based on several values, log each).

> [694c535](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36586/changes/694c535312d90e31f5a3c47f4db7cc32cfbb61c0) _coins: skip compaction if disk space is low_:

Could we add some more explanatory and call-to-action info here? Describing that the uncompacted DB takes up more disk space, and that the user should free up some disk space.
Also, I suggest changing the wording "Skipping" to "Deferring", to suggest that it's not without consequences.
nit: any reason we're not using `CheckDiskSpace()` here?

For an in-memory database, the compaction memory usage problem is arguably even worse than the on-disk one? Since memory-only is quite ephemeral in nature, I think it's uncontroversial to just skip compaction entirely in that case?

`AssumedChainStateSize()` is also rather imprecise here.

I'm not sure we should warn about this. Running on a system with < 2x the chainstate disk space should be supported. If that is the case there is nothing the user can do, and they shouldn't be getting warnings about it.

comments.body:
I don't think this change warrants a release note.
If others disagree, at least the last part of this line should be struck."obsolete data" is not something a user reading the release notes will understand.

> Running on a system with < 2x the chainstate disk space should be supported

We can't expect a node to run without compactions, so we have to let the user know that it's a temporary allowance and that they should do something about it: relocate to a bigger disk, delete some files, prune harder, etc.

comments.body: Do they need to understand more than garbage collection needs a bit more space?

> We can't expect a node to run without compactions

Why not? From my understanding the compactions are just a way to reduce disk usage in the chainstate db, but don't affect node operation otherwise.

Right now the chainstate db is ~11 GB. With pruning we can run it on an instance with < 20 GB of disk space. In this scenario the user will get a warning for every attempted compaction. What is the benefit of having this user relocate to a bigger disk, just to save disk space? Is there a way to determine the total disk size and skip warning if it is < 2x chainstate size?

It might be fine to keep running for a while without regular full compaction, which is why this is a warning rather than an abort. But the operator should be aware that the machine lacks the disk headroom for normal database maintenance.

Allowing tombstones to accumulate can also make full database scans more expensive, since those records still need to be traversed and [skipped](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/20a6babfa9a66f5432ef19c6c433b4357560f853/src/leveldb/db/db_iter.cc#L177).

I don't think we should encourage sizing a node's disk around the chainstate staying at roughly 10 GB (hypothetically, it could even double in a month) - nodes need some headroom, hence the warning.

nit: From commit cef76701a81fde56ad143b4ea559468a6b4dc626 description:
> Skip periodic compaction for in-memory chainstates, which do not need to reclaim disk space.

Maybe here we can more accurately reflect the intention of skipping in-memory chainstates (stated in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36586#discussion_r4357973303). Because if it weren't for compaction's temporary extra space coming out of RAM (even scarcer than disk) and in-memory chainstates being mostly used for short-lived purposes, compaction would also have been helpful to reclaim memory space?

I was wondering whether, if we want the node operator to act on the warning, we could surface it in a more visible/persistent way as well. But it looks like we reserve persistent warnings for more critical/consensus-related cases? (While looking into how we currently emit the more persistent warnings, I also noticed that the first-startup disk space check doesn't account for the space needed by the chainstate, so I opened #36811 to get feedback. If that lands, maybe a follow-up could extend the check with the headroom needed for compaction?)
